pronunciation.notes: Stress falls on the second syllable, nuh. The final r is pronounced in American English; in British English the word ends in a plain, unpronounced-r schwa.

core_idea: Another adds one more of the same kind to a group, or picks out a different member of it.

senses.definition: used before a singular noun for one more of the same kind, in addition to one already mentioned
senses.explanation: Another is a plus other written as one word, so it is never used with a or an in front of it. It can also go before a number and a plural noun to add more of something: another three days.

examples.text: Would you like another cup of coffee?
Could I have another chance to explain?
We need another chair for the table.
The bus was late, so we waited another twenty minutes.

senses.definition: used before a singular noun for a person or thing that is not the one already mentioned or expected
senses.explanation: Here another means a different one, not an additional one: this shirt doesn't fit; let me try another size. It is often used to compare or contrast one case with the next. Another also stands alone, without a noun, in both meanings: from one job to another; I'll have another.

examples.text: This restaurant is full. Let's try another place.
That's another matter we can discuss later.
He left for another job within the same year.
The first plan didn't work, so we tried another approach.

synonym_discrimination.note: Another is one word for a or an plus other and goes directly before a singular noun: another book. Other needs its own determiner before a singular noun: the other book, my other book; before a plural noun, other stands alone: other books.

usage_note: Another is followed by a singular noun, but it can come before a number and a plural noun to mean an additional amount: another two weeks, another five dollars.

learner_errors.incorrect: Can I have an other coffee?
learner_errors.note: Another is always written as a single word, never split into an and other.
Another already contains an, so it is never preceded by a or an.
Another is not used directly after no; use not ... another, or other after no.

adaptation.semantic: Another covers both one more of the same kind and a different one; some languages need two separate words for these ideas.
adaptation.grammar: Another is always one word, usually followed by a singular noun (or by a number and a plural noun: another three days), and is never used with a or an before it, since another already contains an.
